rows.note: Regulatory filings document founder voting control; first-party technical documents describe the Ontology and action architecture.
rows.ceil: layered corporate and customer inference authority
rows.next: Acquire deployment-specific governance, role, action, and customer decision records rather than projecting company governance into every use.
rows.fals: Operative deployments show the vendor or founders have no material role in customer categories or actions.

rows.note: Palantir documentation explicitly describes a digital operational model joining data, logic, security, and actions.
rows.next: Acquire exact deployment schemas, authors, approvals, changes, rejected categories, and represented-person participation.
rows.fals: The relevant system uses no consequential ontology, action type, or category authored through this architecture.

rows.note: The filings establish corporate voting asymmetry; documentation establishes system roles, not subject standing over the mission.
rows.ceil: corporate burden documented, deployment subject burden unresolved
rows.next: Acquire shareholder votes, board disputes, customer appeal rules, subject notices, corrections, and cases in named deployments.
rows.fals: Ordinary shareholders or represented subjects possess and effectively exercise equivalent authority over the relevant objective.

rows.note: The product architecture exposes action rights and privacy controls but cannot establish the practical timing of review in every customer system.
rows.next: Acquire one named deployment from representation through user action, notice, stay, correction, appeal, and outcome.
rows.fals: The relevant deployment contains no consequential action or provides effective pre-action standing.

rows.note: Palantir emphasizes auditability and privacy controls, while the current estate lacks a deployment-specific custody and discoverability matrix.
rows.ceil: generic audit capability, deployment custody unresolved
rows.next: Acquire contracts, data and IP rights, log custody, retention, export, audit, discovery, deletion, and transition records for one deployment.
rows.fals: The customer independently controls and can disclose the complete, portable, versioned record.

rows.note: The filing acknowledges durable founder control and reduced ordinary shareholder influence; no causal claim about performance or abuse follows.
rows.next: Compare governance transitions, votes, proposals, succession, peer firms, performance, and instances where founders lost or shared control.
rows.fals: Ordinary shareholders or independent directors routinely alter the governing objective despite the founder structure.

rows.note: The current record establishes formal founder control and generic action roles, not every exercise or override.
rows.ceil: formal founder and generic customer exception layers
rows.next: Acquire founder votes, reserved matters, board records, deployment overrides, exception reasons, approvals, and audits.
rows.fals: No material exception rights exist or all are effectively constrained by independent actors.

rows.note: Filings document government revenue and founder control; product documents describe operational action; person-level error and private benefit causation remain deployment-specific.
rows.next: Acquire one deployment with exact error, consequence, correction cost, institutional learning, payment, ownership, and gate-shaping chronology.
rows.fals: Complete deployment records show proportionate value, effective subject remedy, and no asymmetric residual benefit.
